focus: Hook the false friend: 'embargo' here is not a trade ban – 'sem embargo de' is a formal/legal connective meaning 'notwithstanding'; quote the card's phrase.
Explain the em + gerund pattern in plain words: 'em sendo assim' is literally 'in being so' – a formal construction English never builds; drop the bare jargon label.

Anchor the culture in the language: this is Antonio Conselheiro's famous sertao/mar prophecy, and 'virar' = 'to turn into' is the everyday become-verb doing the transforming; cut the empty 'about transformation'.
The grammar is the -ao augmentative on a name: Gonzaga -> Gonzagao = 'big Gonzaga', affectionate size-upgrade Portuguese applies to people; keep one clause of who he is, teach the suffix.
Lead with the surprise, not the term 'mesoclisis': in ultra-formal Portuguese the pronoun goes INSIDE the future verb – fazer + se + a = 'far-se-a'; written/legal only, nobody says this aloud.
Hook the false friend: 'prejuizo' normally means loss/harm, not prejudice (that's preconceito) – yet 'sem prejuizo de' is the exact legal calque of English 'without prejudice to'; quote the card.
